observation_summary: The compiler failed to resolve type aliases when they were used in JSDoc annotations before their definitions within a goog.scope block. The existing logic only processed aliases as they were encountered during traversal, which was insufficient for forward references.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves implementing a new 'findAliases' method to pre-scan the scope for all alias definitions before processing the rest of the scope. This is a fundamental change to the procedural strategy of how aliases are identified and resolved, moving from a single-pass traversal to a two-pass approach (or pre-scan). This is a classic algorithmic correction to ensure the necessary data (the alias map) is fully populated before it is needed for type resolution.
evidence_used: The fix adds a new method 'findAliases(t)' to 'ScopedAliases'.
The fix changes the traversal logic to call 'findAliases(t)' at the start of the scope.
The fix refactors the alias validation logic to use the pre-populated 'aliases' map rather than relying on encountering the definition during the standard traversal.
The bug report states: 'Type aliases cannot be used in type annotations before their definitions'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix does not introduce a new design-level capability or class; it modifies the existing alias resolution algorithm within the 'ScopedAliases' pass.
While the fix ensures consistency between alias definitions and usages, the root cause is the procedural order of operations (the algorithm) used to collect those aliases.
